title: When label selection changes the preference estimate
context: CJE is a toolkit for preference modeling and analysis. This contribution asks whether estimates remain stable when the examples selected for human labels change.
contribution: I added an offline sensitivity experiment with six label-selection conditions, 60 labels per policy, and 100 repetitions by default. The notebook reports bias, RMSE, fixed-pool interval coverage, mean interval width, and diagnostic checks.
result: The 100-repetition run produced 600 result records and 18 summary rows; the maintainer independently recomputed the analysis and the pull request merged on November 1, 2026 (UTC; November 2 in UTC+8).
boundary: Positive-propensity conditions are oracle-assisted best cases. The fixed-strata interval procedure is conservative; this is a sensitivity-analysis contribution, not a new estimator or a paper.
evidence: Merged pull request · reproducible notebook · maintainer independent recomputation

title: Keeping ranking scores meaningful at extreme ranks
context: LensKit is a Python toolkit for recommender-system research. Its ordinary rank-biased precision calculation can underflow for relevant items at very deep ranks, and averaging logarithms is not the same as taking the logarithm of the mean score.
contribution: I implemented LogRBP and a log-mean accumulator, with tests covering deep ranks, zero scores, undefined cases, and agreement with ordinary RBP where the latter remains representable. During review, I removed an experimental normalization option at the maintainer’s request.
result: The pull request was merged on October 22, 2026. The accepted implementation preserves the distinction between a defined zero and an undefined score.
boundary: The change does not integrate the new summary into lenskit.tuning, so it is a bounded metric and aggregation contribution rather than a complete resolution of the broader tuning request.
evidence: Merged pull request · implementation and tests · review discussion

title: Validate reward configuration before loading models
context: UniRL (Tencent Hunyuan) is a reinforcement-learning framework with composable reward backends.
contribution: Split reward-graph construction and validation from explicit model loading; forwarded the lifecycle hook through composite backends and kept loading idempotent. The same CPU harness ran 42 checks through real Worker and Hydra construction paths; no GPU training or model-quality improvement is claimed.
result: Merged upstream on October 26, 2026. A matching CPU baseline/fix comparison reported 24/42 checks passing before the fix and 42/42 after it.
boundary: Covers configuration construction and loading lifecycle with fake model loaders; it does not establish GPU training correctness or improved learned policies.

title: Can existing agent traces support same-history preferences?
context: Marin (marin-community) is an open language-model training and research project.
contribution: Added a reproducible feasibility screen for same-history preference pairs from agent traces. It establishes parser-tier action spans and per-turn schema extraction, while documenting why this sample does not establish natural preference pairs. No preference training or model rescoring was run.
result: Merged on October 30, 2026. The screen proved action spans for 123 of 156 completion turns, but did not establish natural preference pairs.
boundary: One trace per task, missing action-level outcomes and pre-action states. No raw unlicensed records are republished, and no preference training or Snowball rescoring was run.
evidence: Merged PR #10741 · aggregate findings · reproduction code

title: When a passing point score is not enough evidence
context: Tapestry (AI Alliance) provides evaluation and governance tooling, including threshold-based evaluation gates.
contribution: Added an opt-in conservative interval policy using runner-supplied bounds. Indeterminate evidence blocks the gate; the existing scalar policy and default configuration hashes remain unchanged. The gate neither estimates nor validates uncertainty intervals.
result: Merged on November 2, 2026 (UTC; November 3 in UTC+8). The public PR reports 31 evaluation tests and eight successful CI checks.
boundary: Uses externally supplied bounds. It does not estimate interval coverage, validate the supplied uncertainty method, or guarantee safe deployment.
evidence: Merged PR #318 · opt-in policy · compatibility tests

title: Does preference scope survive skill mining and deduplication?
context: SkillOpt (Microsoft) mines session evidence into reusable skill candidates.
contribution: Added a CPU-only synthetic paired-session matrix for durable preferences, one-off corrections, reversals and ambiguous feedback through the existing digest/mining/dedup path. Four strict expected failures document evidence-retention gaps. No production persistence policy, model call or learning improvement was implemented.
result: Merged on October 25, 2026 (UTC; October 26 in UTC+8). The targeted run reported 31 passed, four strict expected failures and 130 passing subtests; only eight passing cases and the four expected failures are new in this file.
boundary: Synthetic test-only contribution. Four expected failures expose the proposed retention contract, not production persistence behavior, reliable preference inference or learning gains.
evidence: Merged PR #331 · synthetic contracts · follow-up provenance discussion
